# Introduction

Analytical and microsimulation models are the primary approaches for estimating kinship networks when detailed, long-term demographic data including kinship ties are unavailable. Although both methods use population-level demographic data as inputs, their methodological formulations, assumptions and outputs differ. Analytical models offer mathematical transparency, enabling the calculation of expected values, but are limited in capturing individual variability and interactions. Conversely, microsimulation models simulate demographic events at the individual level, enabling the estimation of the number and distributions of kin, but they are computationally intensive and rely on additional assumptions. Despite their widespread use, systematic comparisons between these approaches remain limited. This study examines the consistency between matrix kinship models and SOCSIM demographic microsimulation when estimating kinship networks under comparable assumptions. Using fertility and mortality data for Sweden (1950-2100) from the [World Population Prospects (WPP) 2024 Revision](https://population.un.org/wpp/downloads?folder=Standard%20Projections&group=CSV%20format), we compared the means and distributions of the numbers and ages of different kin estimated from both models.

# Scripts for reproducible results

**NB**: If you want to re-run the analysis from scratch (i.e., retrieve the data from [WPP](https://population.un.org/wpp/downloads?folder=Standard%20Projections&group=CSV%20format) run the analytical and microsimulation models and reproduce the results), you need R, some standard packages, `DemoKin` and `rsocsim`. 
Please, follow these steps:

1. Download this repository to your computer. 
2. Download and save WPP 2024 data as .csv using the function download_WPP2024(), provided in the script "Functions/Functions_Download_WPP2024.R"
3. Install `DemoKin` from GitHub. Please go to <https://github.com/IvanWilli/DemoKin> to find the instructions on how to install `DemoKin`. 
4. Install `rsocsim` from CRAN using install.packages("rsocsim") 
5. Open the provided RStudio project. 
6. Run the scripts sequentially in the order suggested by the numbers of the files (0-5). 
7. To get exactly the same simulation results, you should use the same randomly generated seed mentioned in script 0.
